_comment: Merge into ~/.claude/settings.json. Uses Windows' built-in curl, which measured ~15 ms per call against ~100-120 ms for a Python forwarder. No quoting needed and no dependency on which Python is on PATH. If beacon-host is not running, curl fails instantly and the hook is a no-op. PreToolUse is deliberately absent: PostToolUse alone covers activity and staleness at half the cost on the busiest event. PostToolBatch is not a duplicate of PostToolUse: it fires once per batch, and it is the only event that arrives when a tool call resolves by being rejected, which is how a row stops being red the moment you answer a prompt with feedback.
_statusline_comment: Optional. The daemon composes the text and returns it in the response body, which curl prints. Omit this block if you already have a status line you like; the beacon works without it, but then it has no source of cost or context data.
